nina_csm: Heads-up: Cedarlake reported degraded tail latency on their support bot overnight. p95 jumped 0.8s -> 1.6s, cost drifting up. They're cost-sensitive and have renewal in 45 days. Proposing a short proactive perf test: compact-int8 model + routing to warm dedicated pool. Thoughts? :thinking:
raf_infra: Sounds reasonable. Need quick metrics: qps, tokens/req, sticky sessions? Any error spike?
nina_csm: qps ~5, tokens/req ~380, sessions sticky. No errors, just tail latency. Customer open to low-risk canary.
priya_se: I can run a 12-prompt eval focused on hallucination-sensitive queries. int8 usually preserves quality with big latency win. If eval looks clean, do a 90min canary routing 70/30.
noah_ops: Routing suggestion: 70% -> rwd-chat-2.0-compact-int8 on dedicated-usw2-warm, 30% -> rwd-chat-2.0 hosted. Ramp 0->70 over 25m, monitor p95, cost delta, and a custom quality check. Auto-rollback if hallucination regressions >4% or p95 worsens.
raf_infra: I'll pre-warm nodes and set kernel to low-latency path. Also enable prefix caching for sessions (TTL 25m).
nina_csm: I'll request 12 sanitized convo turns from Cedarlake by EOD. Priya, can you run the eval once we have them?
priya_se: Yes. Will run and post results. If int8 fails, fallback plan is int8 with conservative quant params or keep hosted model.
ops-bot: Canary scheduled by noah_ops. Window 3340010200 -> 3340011100, ramp 25m. Monitors: p50/p95, tokens_per_req, eval_pass_rate.
noah_ops: Canary started at 3340010200. Halfway (35m): p95=1.0s (down from 1.6s), token cost -24%, eval passrate 100%, no errors.
priya_se: Eval completed: 12 prompts, semantic similarity 0.982, 0 factual regressions, 1 minor formatting diff. Uploading artifacts.
ops-bot: Canary completed at 3340010500. Outcome: success; auto-promote conditions met.
noah_ops: Promoted compact-int8 as primary for dedicated-usw2. Rolling config updated.
nina_csm: Great work. I'll add this to Cedarlake playbook and surface improved economics in upcoming renewal brief. Marking follow-up in 2 weeks to confirm stability. :white_check_mark:
